prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1015; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a parking lot collision in which the insured's vehicle was struck while stopped. The claimant reports a back strain and is represented by counsel, so all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was in force at the time of the loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy period.

Entry 3: Reviewed photographs submitted by the insured. They confirm several details of the scene, though no independent witnesses have come forward. The damage to the vehicle appears consistent with the impact described in the report.

Entry 4: Police records and statements from other parties confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time. The claimant has given the same account of events in every conversation so far. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or inspection records.

Entry 5: Medical records received. The reported back injury fits the kind and force of the collision. No prior injury to the same area appears in the records. Treatment followed a typical course and tapered off as the claimant improved.

Entry 6: Reviewed the file and the medical timeline with the claim supervisor. The injury, vehicle damage, and account are consistent with one another, and no evidence has been found that points away from the reported loss. Claim remains open pending final bills from the treating provider.
